proof_scope: Within the log-star marked window, true signed Picard time differences cancel against every common sign-even Lipschitz function of the full observed history at rate O_B(D^(-B)). This includes moving upper hinges based on the actual source history. It holds uniformly over floors in [0,1] through primes and eligible squares and gives no bound against arbitrary coordinate-dependent or concentrated feasible tests.

The actual endpoint difference has a positive floor-uniform norm lower bound at every positive depth, by strict dissipation between the first two differences and nonexpansiveness. In the marked window each sector carries half its energy up to a vanishing error and, as the floor vanishes, each projected norm has liminf greater than 0.01084468. The specific round-39 RMS sufficient mean increment diverges in both signs throughout this window. There is no lower bound here on the optimal price.

Every real limit curve of the actual physical stationary mark obeys the finite bulk-log cost bound tested by Jacobi mixtures for either sign. Every square curve has right derivative -1/2 at zero, with the field limit taken first. The analogous extremal-sign statement for primes requires saturation of the elementary lower Jacobi extremum.

At every finite field a strictly complementary support chart resolves the real analytic mark at zero, including nonvertex faces. The first derivative is the signed support cardinality difference divided by 2n. The prime affine-support and square uniqueness results give separation at the n^(-1/2) correction to maximal absolute cold slope. No uniform germ radius or common complex domain follows.

For even B <= Q with |B| <= C sqrt(p), the absolute deficit of every quadratic-twisted coset sum from sqrt(p) is uniformly at least a constant times (log log log p)^(1/(4+epsilon)). The argument uses the prime modular Jacobi expansion, Fourier algebra decomposition, and a surviving rational pole. The opposite-cell second moment at a=1 is at least order sqrt(p) times this logarithmic factor. The order-p odd-cell count remains open.

The twisted bound and the earlier untwisted defect exclude flat alternating rectangles of sizes n/sqrt(p)+o((log log log p)^(1/(4+epsilon))) with cross energy above (1/2+gamma)(n/sqrt(p))^3 and gain within o((log log log p)^(1/(4+epsilon))/sqrt(p)) of one.
